Mexico Open: Andrew Novak builds six-shot lead after three rounds at PGA Tour event following stellar Saturday display
Saturday's third round of the Mexico Open sees the USA's Andrew Novak build six-shot lead at PGA Tour event; France's Matthieu Pavon currently sits second in standings; watch live coverage of the final round of the Mexico Open from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday
Sunday 1 November 2026 00:06, UK
Andrew Novak built a comfortable lead at the turn and then poured it on by going five under par on the first five holes of the back nine on his way to a nine-under 62 as he built a six-shot lead at the Mexico Open.
About the only thing Novak did wrong at Vidanta Vallarta was losing the handle on a club twirl at the par-five 12th while admiring a 279-yard shot that settled 20 feet away for an eagle.
That was part of his sublime stretch of three birdies and an eagle that extended his lead to seven shots. It was such a great day for Novak that even when he had a lie in the rough with a golf ball well below his feet, he hammered that out to six feet on the 14th for a birdie.
Novak ended the day on a 23-under 190, primed for his first individual title on the PGA Tour. His only other victory was teaming with Ben Griffin in the Zurich Classic of New Orleans last year.
He had the low round of the day while playing in the last group, and goes into the final round coming off scores of 61-62.
"Very much the same, maybe a little sloppy at the end," Novak said of the two rounds. "But the putter saved it."
He holed a six-foot par on the 16th and made a 10-foot par putt on the 17th after coming up short.
Matthieu Pavon of France birdied his last two holes for a 65 to get within six shots. Doug Ghim had a 64 and was another shot behind.
"It makes it easier for me to be in my own bubble because I know that something significant would probably need to happen for me to have a chance tomorrow," Ghim said. "I'll do my best to put any pressure on him and see what happens."
Pavon needs something special, too, though he already is having a good week if he can hold his position. His two-year exemption from winning at Torrey Pines in 2024 runs out this year. Pavon came to the Mexico Open at No 140 in the FedEx Cup. A runner-up finish would move him just inside the top 100.
Kihei Akina, a 20-year-old, settled down after a bogey-bogey start and posted a 68. He was nine shots behind in a tie for seventh. Another finish in the top 10 would give him another point in the PGA Tour University accelerated program.
Everyone is chasing Novak, who has made only three bogeys through 54 holes.
"You want to back up a really low round with something low, but you don't usually expect that," Novak said.
"You expect usually there's going to be some give, and you've just got to be patient with it the next day. I still kind of came out firing today, was throwing some darts, making putts and trying to stay out of my own way."
Watch live coverage of the PGA Tour's Mexico Open final round from 8pm on Sky Sports Golf on Sunday.

הגולפאי האמריקאי אנדרו נובאק ביסס את מעמדו במקום הראשון באליפות מקסיקו פתוחה במסגרת סבב ה-PGA, לאחר שסיים את הסיבוב השלישי בתוצאה של תשע מתחת לתקן. נובאק רשם רצף מרשים שכלל מספר ציפורים (בירדיז) ונשר (איגל) באתגרים המרכזיים של המסלול.

במקום השני בטבלה נמצא הצרפתי מתייה פאבון, שצמצם את הפער בעזרת סיום חזק ביומו השלישי של הטורניר, בעוד שדאג גקים דולק אחריהם. נובאק נכנס ליום המנוחות האחרון כשהוא ממוקם ביתרון בטוח של שש חבטות לקראת זכייה אפשרית בתואר היחידים הראשון שלו בסבב המקצועני.
